sections.h2: Who runs Lucas County property tax
sections.html:
The work splits between two county offices located together at One Government Center in Toledo. The Auditor sets values, keeps the tax records, accepts Board of Revision complaints and takes homestead applications. Reach the Auditor at 419-213-4406. The Treasurer, in Suite 500, mails the bills, collects what is owed and deals with delinquent parcels.

Which city or village and which school district your parcel sits in decides most of the bill. The county had 423,347 people as of July 2025 and 201,974 housing units. The typical owned home is worth $163,900, owners hold 62.0 percent of homes, and monthly gross rent is $934 at the median.

The Auditor's All About Property Taxes guide describes two steps. First, the property's market value is converted to a 35 percent assessed value. Second, that assessed value is multiplied by the tax rate for the taxing district and divided by 1,000.

Levies that voters approve set the rate, and appraisers have no say in it. A bill paid in 2026 covers tax year 2025, because real property is taxed a year behind.

Two older state credits exist, a 10 percent non-business credit and a 2.5 percent owner-occupied credit. Neither applies to levies passed after 2014, including replacement levies, so they do not cut the whole bill by those percentages. Look at your bill to see what credits it shows.

The bill itself lists each levy for your school district, city or village, county and other districts. Because a seller's bill is always a year behind, a house that was just improved or just sold may show a tax that does not yet reflect that change.

Lucas County bills come in two installments, and the dates are printed right on the bill. Treasurer staff post the coming date once the bills go out. Under section 323.17, a delayed tax duplicate can push the payment dates to January 31 and July 20, so the dates are not identical every year.

Paying by mail is where people get caught. A USPS postmark can carry a date a day or more after you drop the envelope, and Ohio law treats the postmark as the payment date. The Treasurer offers three workarounds:

  • Send the check well before the due date.
  • Ask for a hand-stamped postmark at the post office counter.
  • Pay online, which is available at any time.

A payment plan option is also available. Ask the Treasurer's office for the terms before you fall behind.

The Board of Revision takes complaints starting January 1 and ending at the close of March. The board has three seats: Auditor, Treasurer and one Commissioner, or their delegates. It hears disputes about value and nothing else, so levy and rate complaints go elsewhere.

Lucas County Board of Revision steps
StepWhat to do
Filing windowJanuary 1 to March 31
FormDTE Form 1, 1M or 2, filed on paper (notarized) or online
Hearing30-minute slot, in person, by phone or by video
EvidenceSubmit at least 5 days before the hearing
AttendanceRecommended, not required
Further appealBoard of Tax Appeals or Court of Common Pleas, 30 days counted from the date the decision was mailed

The burden is on you. Bring nearby comparable sales, your own recent purchase price or a private appraisal. For a house damaged or torn down, a separate DTE 26 application adjusts value starting the next tax year.

sections.h2: What happens to your tax while a complaint is pending
sections.html:
You may pay based on your own figure. Section 5715.19 requires the Treasurer to accept a payment computed on the value stated in your complaint while the complaint is pending. If the final value turns out higher than what you paid, interest runs on the shortfall from the original due date, so keep the complaint number handy when you pay.

Four more points from the statute:

  • The filing window stays open to the later of March 31 or the close of first-half collection.
  • After the last filing day the board has 180 days to decide.
  • Filing again on the same parcel in the same interim period takes a changed fact, such as an arm's length sale, storm or fire loss, or a major improvement.
  • Papers you hold back from the board may be barred if you appeal later.

If you plan to sell this year, a pending complaint can still matter to the buyer. Give the title company the complaint number and the value you stated, since the tax that was paid at that figure may be adjusted once the board rules.

Lucas County offers homestead relief in four forms. An owner who is 65 or older, or totally and permanently disabled, can claim it on the house they live in when 2025 taxable income was $41,000 or less. A spouse's taxable income counts toward that cap, though Social Security does not. Owners rated or compensated at 100 percent for a service-connected disability qualify without an income limit. Surviving spouses of first responders killed in the line of duty can qualify for an enhanced version.

For tax year 2025, payable in 2026, the exempted value is $29,000, and that amount doubles for the service-connected disability and surviving spouse tracks. It reduces taxable value on your primary residence and nothing else. Questions go to Homestead@co.lucas.oh.us or 419-213-4406.

When the home sells, Ohio's value statement asks the buyer to confirm with the seller whether the property carries these reductions or the agricultural use valuation, as section 319.202 requires. Answer it accurately, since a reduction may end with the sale.

Deeds pass through the Auditor before recording. The Auditor's transfer fact sheet lists $0.50 per parcel plus $4.00 for each $1,000 of price. Death, survivorship and own-trust transfers are generally exempt from the larger charge.

Unpaid tax stays attached to the parcel, so get the Treasurer's balance for yours before signing a contract. At closing the title company pays what is owed from your proceeds. A cash buyer can move fast, but the balance still has to be cleared before the deed is recorded. Ask the Treasurer or your title agent for a payoff figure a few days before closing, and bring your latest bill and parcel number to the table. If a Board of Revision complaint is pending, tell the title company so the payment is figured on the right number.

faqs.q: By what date must I contest a Lucas County value?
faqs.a: March 31. The Board of Revision accepts complaints from January 1 through March 31. State law allows the later date of March 31 or the close of first-half collection for the tax year.

faqs.q: Can the Lucas County Board of Revision lower my tax rate?
faqs.a: No. The board hears appeals on property values only, not on the taxes themselves. Levy rates come from votes in your taxing district.

faqs.q: How do I prove a Lucas County value is wrong?
faqs.a: Bring evidence such as comparable neighborhood sales, a recent sale of the property or a private appraisal. The burden of proof sits with the owner who files.

faqs.q: Who qualifies for the Lucas County homestead exemption?
faqs.a: Homeowners aged 65 or more, or totally and permanently disabled, who live in the house and had $41,000 or less in 2025 taxable income. Owners rated 100 percent disabled through military service and surviving spouses of first responders killed on duty also qualify, with a larger exempted amount.

faqs.q: Is a postmarked check still safe for a Lucas County tax payment?
faqs.a: Not always. USPS postmarks can show a later date than the day you mail, and Ohio law uses the postmark date. Pay online or request a hand-stamped postmark.
